description:
FILED s543a (Opus, 2026-11-16), found while reading the Log-Log4perl board rows that line tracking did NOT fix (scratch/s543a/probes/l4p/ in the s543a worktree).  Since s543a `caller` answers perl's file and line in the default build, yet Log::Log4perl's PatternLayout still prints `[undef]` for %F %L %C and the wrong sub for %M.  Two causes, both #233 residue (docs/caller-implementation.md "What is not kept"), neither a location problem:

(b) AN ANONYMOUS SUB IS NOT A FRAME unless its body reads one (s539d: +3.5 ns per anonymous call, left out).  Log4perl's level methods (`$logger->debug`) and the Logger's dispatch closure are anonymous subs; the layout reads `caller($caller_offset)` (Layout/PatternLayout.pm:200) and `caller($caller_offset + 1)` for %M, with the offset counted in PERL's frames.  PCL has two fewer, so caller() runs past the outermost frame and answers the empty list.
    PROBE depth.pl (render wrapped to list every caller($i); the program has no `use warnings`):
      perl: 0:PatternLayout::__ANON__@206/bm 1:Appender::log@299/bm 2:Logger::__ANON__@784/bm 3:Logger::__ANON__@13/bm  -> F=depth.pl L=13
      PCL : 0:PatternLayout::__ANON__@205/nobm 1:Appender::log@290/nobm                                                 -> F=[undef] L=[undef]
    PROBE anon.pl (`*L::debug = sub { render() }`, render reads caller(1) / caller(2)):
      perl: c1=L::__ANON__ line=5 c2=undef / c1=L::__ANON__ line=4 c2=main::mysub
      PCL : c1=undef line=undef c2=undef   / c1=main::mysub line=6 c2=undef

(a) THE WARNINGS BITMASK (field 9) is undef in every PCL frame; PatternLayout.pm:205 replaces EVERY field with '[undef]' `unless (defined $bitmask)` ("caller() choked because of a whacko caller level").  perl's bitmask is defined at every frame of the probe above (bm), and in a plain program exactly when the call site is under `use warnings` (bm.pl: no pragma -> undef; `use warnings` -> "\x55" x 20; `use strict` alone -> undef, hints 2018; PCL: hints, bitmask, hinthash all undef).  So even with (b) fixed, the layout would still print [undef] until field 9 is defined where perl's is.
    PROBE l4p.pl (layout "F=%F L=%L M=%M C=%C", one call from top level and one from `sub mysub`):
      perl: F=l4p.pl L=10 M=main:: C=main      / F=l4p.pl L=9 M=main::mysub C=main
      PCL : F=[undef] L=[undef] M=main:: C=[undef] (both lines; the same without `use warnings`)

WHAT A FIX NEEDS (not designed here): (b) is #233's "a frame for every anonymous sub" (measured and left out at s539d), or a narrower rule -- an anonymous sub that is INSTALLED (assigned to a glob) or that calls a named sub is a frame; (a) a per-call-site constant for the bitmask's DEFINEDNESS, which is what Log4perl tests ("\x55" x N under any `use warnings`, perl's value elsewhere -- measure what a frame inside a module under `use warnings` answers); the bits themselves are the warnings model PCL does not have (#221).  Both together are what the Log4perl rows need; either alone moves none of them.

ROWS: the Log-Log4perl board rows keyed NS:ns-caller-fidelity that stayed failing after s543a (003Layout 004Config 005Config-Perl 007LogPrio 020Easy 022Wrap 024WarnDieCarp 027Watch2 033UsrCspec 045Composite 051Extra 059Wrapper), each re-noted in baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv with this task.
subject: Log::Log4perl %F %L %C %M still wrong after line tracking went on (s543a): the logger's anonymous subs push no frame, so caller($offset) runs past PCL's frames, and caller's warnings bitmask (field 9) is always undef, which PatternLayout reads as 'caller choked' -> [undef]
